title: Naturality of the prescribed common-stage pullback compositor
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Z\xrightarrow{h}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ be arbitrary composable scheme morphisms, with $\ell$ invertible on all three schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the rational and common-stage categories, pullback functors and their prescribed operation maps [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and the component compositor $c_{f,h;K}$ with its every-field representative normalization [def-pod-rational-common-pullback-composition]. For any common-stage objects $K,N$ and arbitrary arrow $a:K\to N$, one has $F_{hf}(a)\,c_{f,h;N}=c_{f,h;K}\,F_h(F_f(a))$. Thus the prescribed component compositor family is natural. No isomorphism hypothesis on $f$ or $h$ and no faithful-transition assumption are imposed.

source.place: Step 5, operation transports; rational/common-stage descent in the coefficient-descent refinement.

proof.text: For a localized morphism, induct on its scalar-first tensor expression. The zero and sum cases follow from additivity of the recorded rational pullback functors. On a pure tensor, their prescribed map formulas and the prescribed rational compositor identify both routes with the same scalar tensor the two integral compositor naturality routes. Apply integral naturality. This treats every localized arrow, not just arrows admitting an integral lift.

Represent the common-stage morphism over a single finite coefficient field using the common-stage Hom induction principle. The prescribed pullback map and compositor representative equations express both sides of naturality at this field. Expand functoriality and cancel each comparison followed by its inverse. The remaining equation is precisely rational compositor naturality. Apply the common-stage class map, which preserves compositions, to obtain the asserted equality. This uses no faithfulness of transition functors and no extra condition on the schemes or on the morphisms.

lean.statement:
theorem commonStagePullbackComposition_naturality
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [_root_.Algebra (Padic l) Ω]
    [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)]
    [∀ y : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField y)]
    [∀ z : Z, Invertible (l : Z.residueField z)] (f : X ⟶ Y) (h : Z ⟶ X)
    {K N : generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω Y} (a : K ⟶ N) :
    (commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω (h ≫ f)).map a ≫
        (pullbackTensorCommonComposition l Ω f h N).hom =
      (pullbackTensorCommonComposition l Ω f h K).hom ≫
        (commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω h).map ((commonStageDerivedPullback l Ω f).map a)
